title.value: GitHub Repositories with Links to Academic Papers: Public Access, Traceability, and Evolution
title.justification: The paper is focused on exploring the links between GitHub repositories and academic papers, specifically looking at public access, traceability, and evolution.
title.quote: Traceability between published scientific breakthroughs and their implementation is essential, especially in the case of open-source scientific software which implements bleeding-edge science in its code.

extractions.description: This paper investigates the role of linking GitHub repositories with academic papers, focusing on public access, traceability, and the evolution of these links. The study involves analyzing 20,000 GitHub repositories to understand the relationship and impact of academic paper references within, and examines how updates and traceability affect scientific communication and software development.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's primary focus is on the traceability of academic papers and software development through GitHub, which is not a central theme related to sustainable development or environmental issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: While the role of traceability between scientific artifacts can be important for the above reasons, there is no existing work investigating the current practice of creating and maintaining such trace links.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate, ecology, or sustainable development but rather on academic traceability and software documentation practices.
primary_category.quote: Our work is situated in the literature on (1) traceability among different scientific artifacts and (2) the references in open source software documentation.

secondary_categories.justification: The study does not address any other categories related to sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We conduct a large-scale study of 20 thousand GitHub repositories that make references to academic papers.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category related to sustainable development covered in this paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: Traceability between published scientific breakthroughs and their implementation is essential, especially in the case of open-source scientific software.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not delve into any additional sub-categories pertinent to sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This paper’s contributions are three-fold: (i) a large-scale and comprehensive study of 20 thousand links to establish the frequency of links from GitHub repositories to academic papers, (ii) a mixed-methods study to identify public access, traceability, and evolutionary aspects of such links and (iii) availability of an online appendix, which contains our qualitative coding results in this study.

applications.value: Understanding academic traceability and evolution in software repositories.
applications.justification: This application is the core theme of the study, examining how academic papers are referenced within GitHub repositories and how these references evolve.
applications.quote: Our findings indicate that machine learning-related repositories, especially deep learning, are the most frequent among GitHub repositories with links to academic papers.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not propose a new category centered on sustainable development as it focuses on academic paper traceability.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is necessary as the paper's focus is not on creating sustainable development categories.
